key_insight: Ionic concentration gradients reorganize supramolecular polymers into spatial zones with locally enhanced assembly dynamics, and those local dynamics are largely governed by the local ionic environment rather than the global average composition.
engineering_relevance: This suggests chemical gradients can be used as a design handle to program where and how synthetic supramolecular materials assemble, adapt, or move in heterogeneous environments.
method: Constant chemical potential MD (CμMD) to impose ionic gradients
Comparison of two prototypical supramolecular polymer models under gradient vs homogeneous conditions
evidence_signal: The abstract reports molecular-resolution simulation results showing pronounced spatial reorganization and local quasi-equilibria across two models, enabling a single gradient simulation to represent a continuum of local chemical environments.
watch_item: The conclusions are simulation-based and depend on coarse-grained/implicit-solvent assumptions, so experimental validation and parameter transferability should be checked before device-level deployment.
paper_title: Ionic gradients shape the spatial organization and dynamics of supramolecular polymers
